newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, blue chips to rise.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, blue chips to rise.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Wednesday in somewhat slower trade, but analysts predicted growth in leading issues amid renewed interest of foreign investors.
"The situation is slowly getting back to normal. Foreign buyers are calling up again," said Igor Kos of Taurus brokerage.
He predicted new gains for drugs firm Pliva, Zagrebacka Banka and food processor Podravka.
"They are to serve as a barometer for other stocks, which will follow (the trend)," he said but added that trade could remain slow until the prices stabilised.
Of seven issues that traded, four rose, one fell and two were unchanged. Volume shrank to 7,739 units and turnover was halved at 7.7 million kuna.
Top gainer hotelier Laguna rose 60 kuna to 1,010 on a volume of 82 shares. Another hotelier Jadranturist also added 15 kuna to 235, trading 167 shares.
Pliva recovered 250 kuna to 13,450, selling 199 units. Its GDRs traded at $49.75-$49.875 in London.

The only decliner, Zagrebacka Banka, edged down 21 kuna to close at 1,004. But it was the most actively traded issue on a volume of 4,071 shares. The bank's E-series was flat at 430 kuna, with 55 shares sold.
Confectioner Kras rose 10 kuna to 400 on a rebound, with 902 shares traded.
Podravka remained unchanged at 220 kuna, with 2,263 shares changing hands.
